arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Prelogar argued Congress did not want equitable tolling to apply.
Mr. Rosenkranz argued the administrative presentment requirement supports the government's position.
Justice Roberts asked if modern statutes would interpret similar words as jurisdictional bars.
Justice Scalia asked if prior notions of congressional intent were wrong at the time.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks if the equitable tolling doctrine applies to the Federal Tort Claims Act statute of limitations. The government argues Congress intended a strict deadline. The plaintiff argues equitable principles should allow extensions.

paragraphs: This case determines whether federal employees face strict deadlines for personal injury claims. It clarifies the scope of sovereign immunity waivers. It affects how courts interpret statutory time limits involving the government.
